stories.title: The one change that worked: I deleted Instagram – and embraced the joys of a truly private life
summary: I self-righteously refused to download TikTok, declared Snapchat to be for “children”, and posted less regularly on Instagram than half of the people I followed.As I went through my university years, however, certain changes crept up on me.
I began to swap reading – or essay-writing – for hours spent curating new posts.
What usually followed was a night of reloading my feed to see how many people had reacted to my post – or worse, hadn’t reacted at all.

stories.title: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
summary: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times.
Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years agoA few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about.
But despite the fact it now has been consulted trillions of times by billions of people (English Wikipedia alone is 5.2bn words long), it inspires an odd lack of curiosity.

stories.title: What are self-replicating ‘AI worms’, and why is Anthropic worried about them?
summary: The red team, as such internal testers are called, said it created a malicious AI program that spread autonomously through internet-connected “smart” televisions and could do the same inside other ordinary devices.

While machines running AI usually need a fair amount of computing power, the researchers said that their program split parts of itself among 15 televisions and was still able to function by using a bit of power from each.

summary: From science kits to karaoke machines, shower sets to brain-boosting games, here are the presents our mini testers loved the most• The best gifts for seven-year-oldsEight is such a wonderful age.

Kids are old enough to have their own interests and hobbies, but still young enough to get swept up in play and be absorbed for hours if you find the right toy for them.By eight, children’s interests and skills are taking shape.
And while they think they’re extremely grown up, eight-year-olds still need plenty of time to play for their overall wellbeing.

stories.title: World Bank says ‘small AI’ could transform developing countries
summary: Bank’s chief knowledge officer says the tech could speed up economic development from centuries to decadesThe World Bank is urging developing countries to kickstart the creation of “small AI” models, which can run on a mobile phone with low connectivity, to reap the full benefits of artificial intelligence.While Silicon Valley big tech firms are focused on ever more sophisticated consumer products, Paschal Donohoe, the World Bank’s chief knowledge officer, said AI could also accelerate development for emerging economies – but only if it was adapted to local needs.
